description: Find electric vehicles by brand or model name, or list the whole catalog ranked for a use case, optionally only those with at least a given range. Use it first whenever you have a name but no slug, and for questions like 'which EVs go furthest' or 'best family EV'. Returns JSON: per model the slug (pass it to get_model or compare_models), brand, name, score out of 100 for the chosen preset (score_tier says whether every input is verified), official range in km with its test cycle (range_km_official + range_cycle: WLTP, EPA, CLTC or NEDC) and the comparable WLTP-equivalent figure, DC charging 10-80 % in minutes, battery kWh, each of these with its source and verification status, markets where it is sold, the number of known versions, the page URL and the cover photo with its credit. Prices are per market and per version: read them with get_model. Paged: total, page, total_pages.

limit.description: Models per page (default 20, at most 50 without an API key).

min_range_km.description: Only EVs whose official range is at least this many kilometres on the comparable WLTP-equivalent basis (an EPA or CLTC figure is converted by its cycle factor). For miles, multiply by 1.609.

page.description: Page number, 1-based (default 1); see total_pages in the answer.

preset.description: What the ranking optimizes for (default everyday): everyday (a balanced daily driver — range, charging and practicality); long_range (maximum distance per charge for road trips); family (space, seats and practicality for a family); performance (acceleration and fast-charging capability); city (a short, easy-to-park car that still charges fast); winter (range that survives the cold — ranked on our own winter estimate).

query.description: Words of the brand and/or model name, any order, case-insensitive; every word must match, e.g. 'tesla 3', 'ioniq', 'bmw ix'. Omit to rank the whole catalog.

name: search_models

hint.description: Why a page is empty and what to try.

terms.description: Terms the data is given under.

title: Search and rank EVs
